children: on Thursday said it plans to invest more than $100 million to build an advanced manufacturing facility in Greenwood, Indiana, expanding its U.S. production capacity and creating 300 skilled jobs.

The 585,000-square-foot facility is expected to begin operations by 2028 and will make equipment used in Amazon’s fulfillment and robotics network across North America. The jobs will include manufacturing, engineering, quality assurance and program management positions, with average annual pay of nearly $100,000, according to the company.

expands its use and production of robots in its operations. The company said it has manufactured well over 1 million robots in the U.S., with the machines deployed across more than 300 facilities and involved in 75% of customer orders.

said it has invested more than $40 billion in Indiana since 2008 and supports more than 27,000 direct jobs in the state. It has invested more than $230 billion in U.S. manufacturing since 2010, according to the company.
The Greenwood project follows an August announcement of another robotics manufacturing investment in Texas. Amazon
currently operates two robotics manufacturing facilities in Massachusetts.
The company said the Indiana site will include fabrication, robotic welding, automated powder coating and assembly operations, along with AI-powered manufacturing systems.
